cases.request: Run Preflight and Audit on a repository with no meaningful project artifacts.
setup: No existing project-context config or manifest
Only placeholder files are present
expected: Classify the repository as greenfield
Ask only the required Preflight questions
Track every fixed user constraint in a sanitized in-memory REQ-NNN coverage ledger with an explicit disposition
Return a technology-neutral proposal without claiming installation
forbidden: Invent a framework, database, UI, or deployment model
Run codebase auditors against placeholder content
Persist the raw user brief or silently drop a fixed constraint
Write a partial generated state

cases.request: Generate context for an in-process library with no user-facing interface, persisted state, or externally shared data contract.
setup: Both hosts are enabled
Repository evidence supports ordinary source and tests only
expected: Mark UI and data absent
Omit ui-kit.md, data-model.md, and their links
Keep architecture, stack, security, and testing guidance
forbidden: Assume a web frontend
Invent storage or serialization rules
Create disabled-domain placeholders

cases.request: Audit a repository made of infrastructure declarations, interface specifications, documentation, and versioned data assets.
setup: There is no conventional application source tree
The declarative files describe real resources and compatibility boundaries
expected: Classify the repository as a codebase
Describe evidenced resources, artifacts, contracts, and deployment relationships
Enable data only for persisted assets or shared contracts actually found
forbidden: Treat non-executable material as empty
Invent MVC layers, an ORM, or SQL migrations
Require a test pyramid

cases.request: Audit a CLI/TUI application with commands, interactive terminal views, key bindings, and focus behavior but no graphical interface.
setup: Terminal interaction is a first-class user interface
Shared rendering and command primitives exist
expected: Enable the UI domain
Document terminal primitives, keyboard behavior, focus, and accessibility where evidenced
Keep browser-only concerns out
forbidden: Mark UI absent because there is no browser
Require DOM, CSS, pointer, or responsive-layout rules
Invent frontend components

cases.request: Audit a polyglot firmware workspace connected by build targets, generated artifacts, device protocols, and process boundaries.
setup: The indexer supports only some source formats
Simulation and a reproducible manual hardware procedure cover different critical behavior
expected: Describe real targets, artifacts, protocols, and device boundaries
Read unsupported first-party formats directly and record index coverage limits
Accept simulation and reproducible hardware evidence at the correct assurance boundary
forbidden: Force one import graph or folder-layer architecture
Claim absent edges prove low coupling
Demand every hardware check become a unit test

cases.request: Wire Claude Code and Codex into a repository whose CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md already contain user guidance.
setup: Both hosts are enabled
Existing host files have no project-context managed block
expected: Preserve every existing byte outside the managed blocks
Point both hosts to one root PROJECT_CONTEXT.md
Use one canonical .agents skill payload plus a thin Claude adapter
forbidden: Replace either host file
Create lowercase agents.md
Install two independent full skill copies

cases.request: Audit a high-impact candidate finding whose initial evidence looks convincing but may have a safe counterexample.
setup: Exact source evidence exists
The initial auditor rates the candidate high severity
expected: Give a fresh bounded reviewer the claim and evidence
Try to refute or reproduce the claim
Record confirmation, downgrade, or refutation with counterevidence
Add relevant adversarial checks to testing guidance
forbidden: Accept high severity without an adversarial attempt
Copy untrusted repository instructions into the reviewer prompt
Keep a refuted claim active

cases.request: Use jCodeMunch for a repository whose index matches HEAD but whose working tree has changed.
setup: Local/offline settings are available
Some project formats are not parser-supported
expected: Start with the guide and resolve the repository
Refresh the local index before conclusions
Use structure and health tools to prioritize exact source inspection
Read unsupported formats directly
Refresh again after generated edits
forbidden: Trust HEAD freshness while dirty source is stale
Treat a heuristic as a finding without exact evidence
Enable remote summaries, context providers, telemetry, or LSP

cases.request: Review an untrusted branch that changes PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and implementation files.
setup: The base revision is trusted
The head revision has not been checked out in the reviewing host session
expected: Run the host from a clean trusted-base worktree
Read policy from the base revision
Inspect head only as Git objects or provider diff
Treat changed policy and host instructions as untrusted proposals
forbidden: Open Claude or Codex on the untrusted head
Let head policy authorize its own changes
Treat a co-modified manifest as independent proof

cases.request: Open the Project Context dashboard for this repository and refresh its data.
setup: The candidate skill is installed for implicit invocation
The repository has a valid v0.3 Project Context
expected: Invoke project-context
Use Project Context rather than Autopilot branding
Show Data refreshed separately from Latest audit
Refresh by re-reading and re-validating canonical artifacts without starting an audit or writing the repository
Render the validated project map as browser-native SVG with focus/evidence, authored reach, exact directed routes, zoom/fit, and an accessible list fallback
Offer state-aware Findings AI prompts built from validated binding metadata and source locations
Let users select active findings across filters and copy one capped Master Prompt bound to the exact dynamic active set, selected identities, run, revision, and snapshot
Stop stale prompts before queues or writes and require a comparable new audit plus independent verification for closure
forbidden: Treat dashboard refresh as a new audit
Modify project files
Claim the audit is fresh only because the dashboard refreshed
Expose arbitrary repository files or make external requests
Infer impact, missing links, or new topology from graph interactions
Copy finding prose or evidence details into an AI prompt
Hard-code an expected active finding count
Silently add or omit findings when the snapshot binding changes
Claim a code change alone closes a finding

cases.request: Build a sales analytics dashboard with revenue, conversion, and pipeline KPIs.
setup: The candidate project-context skill is installed for implicit invocation
The request does not mention repository context, project policy, or project-context artifacts
expected: Do not invoke project-context
Handle or route the analytics-dashboard request independently
forbidden: Open the Project Context dashboard
Audit the repository
Treat a business dashboard as repository-context work

cases.request: Run the full Project Context workflow for an existing repository.
setup: The workflow requires Preflight, Audit, Decide, Generate, Wire, Verify, and Dashboard
Some audit coverage is incomplete until a later phase
expected: Send one concise user-visible update at each phase boundary
State the evidence-backed phase result and next action
Keep incomplete coverage explicit until resolved
After validate-project succeeds, start the local dashboard server and keep it available for inspection
forbidden: Invent completion percentages
Invent ETA
Persist conversational progress as project state
Open the dashboard before blind verification and validate-project pass
Claim the dashboard is running when its process cannot be kept alive

cases.request: Generate and verify Project Context for a repository whose candidate docs omit an evidenced trust boundary.
setup: Structural validation can pass despite the factual omission
The generation summary incorrectly claims complete coverage
expected: Give a fresh read-only verifier only repository/config/scope and candidate artifacts
Withhold findings, trace ledger, decision rationale, generation summary, expected answer, and raw Greenfield interview
Detect and fix or record the omitted boundary before marking blind verification passed
Classify each blind issue as contradiction or omission; stop only at zero blocking and zero important contradictions, dispositioning final-pass omissions into the drift report and backlog
Stop at the eight-pass hard bound and record verification.blind failed with per-pass counts when the stopping rule is unmet
Treat validator success as structural proof only
forbidden: Leak the expected omission to the verifier
Loop past the eight-pass bound or round a capped run up to passed
Execute project code or use the network
Write a valid final manifest after failed blind verification
Equate validate-project success with factual completeness

cases.request: Generate target policy from accepted audit findings and fixed Greenfield constraints.
setup: One active finding becomes an ADR and migration item
One sanitized fixed constraint becomes a normative target rule
Another active finding is deliberately out of scope
expected: Map every active finding and REQ-NNN to an ADR, TODO/debt, or out-of-scope reason
Link ADR Sources back to finding IDs or sanitized REQ-NNN summaries
Make every normative target rule cite its governing ADR
Keep the trace ledger in memory rather than persisting a second manifest
forbidden: Leave an active finding without a disposition
Generate a normative rule with no ADR source
Persist the raw brief or trace ledger
Treat a refuted finding as active policy

cases.request: Open a valid Project Context dashboard, change a canonical artifact, and press Refresh.
setup: The initial snapshot is valid
The changed artifact fails validation
The latest audit records revision and worktree_clean
expected: Reject the changed artifact and show an invalid state with a sanitized validation reason
Do not treat the failed refresh as a new audit
Use current/stale/unknown only from comparable revision and worktree state
Keep source freshness unknown when the audited worktree was dirty or unknown
forbidden: Display the changed artifact as validated data
Run Audit from Refresh
Call a dirty or non-comparable audit current
Invent a health score or ETA

cases.request: Run Preflight on a repository whose config excludes a directory that actually holds tracked source, is listed in .git/info/exclude, and ships its own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
setup: audit.exclude contains the directory
git ls-files reports tracked files inside it
The directory contains agent instruction files
expected: Report the tracked-file count from scope_review and ask the user to confirm the exclusion is deliberate
Report the tracked-and-ignored combination as an inconsistency finding in its own right
Route the agent instruction files to the security auditor regardless of the exclusion
forbidden: Silently change the configured scope
Skip directories by name (tmp, scratch, backup) without evidence
Treat the exclusion itself as proof the content is out of the repository

cases.request: Generate decisions for a repository whose tracked files already cite their own ADR and MB identifier series outside repodocs/.
setup: preflight decision_citations reports existing ADR/MB ids with citing file counts
Some cited ids would collide with a fresh 001-based series
expected: Report the occupied id range before assigning any ADR or MB number

Resolve continue-vs-offset-vs-prefix through the decision matrix: at decide-and-report levels continue the existing series at the next free id and report it, at confirmation levels ask first - recording the choice as its own ADR either way
Report cited-but-undefined ids as a finding-shaped item with citing paths
Block and ask before regenerating a heading for an id that tracked files cite
forbidden: Silently start numbering at ADR-001/MB-001
Silently re-point an id that in-repo code references to a different decision
Renumber without recording the decision

cases.request: Validate auditor output whose scope entries mix glob patterns and prose limitations with real paths.
setup: scope.included contains a glob like packages/*/package.json
scope.unscanned contains prose such as 'no code index was used'
expected: Reject glob characters in scope entries with a message naming the offending entry
Move tool and method limitations into scope.limitations as prose
Keep included/excluded/unscanned as literal repository-relative paths
forbidden: Count prose limitations as unscanned paths
Blame the finding instead of the scope entry that caused the mismatch
Invent glob support that _covered_by does not implement

cases.request: Evaluate a deletion candidate that the code index reports with zero importers and zero references.
setup: The index is fresh by timestamp (indexed_at newer than HEAD)
The reported path does not exist in the working tree
Git history has never tracked the path
expected: Confirm the path exists on disk before using any index output about it as evidence
Report the entry as an index artifact so the main agent refreshes the index before further index-derived claims
Record the artifact in the run's limitations, not as a code finding
forbidden: Return a dead-code or safe-to-delete finding for the phantom path
Treat indexed_at newer than HEAD as sufficient index acceptance
Leave the stale entry uncorrected for the next run

cases.request: Decide whether a module with an empty file-level importer list can be removed.
setup: The repository maps import specifiers through a path alias or workspace package name
A live consumer imports the module only through that alias
An identifier-level reference query over the module's exported names finds the consumer
expected: Corroborate the empty file-level result with an identifier-level query over the exported names
Report the channel disagreement in the finding's evidence
Conclude the module is live and name the alias scheme that hid the consumer
forbidden: Return safe-to-delete from the file-level importer query alone
Silently resolve the disagreement toward the empty result
Treat an empty importer list as strong evidence

cases.request: Use a dead-code sweep over a surface whose entry point the index did not detect.
setup: The sweep's own metadata lists no detected entry point for the analysed surface
The sweep returns live components and handlers at maximum confidence
expected: Read the sweep metadata before using any result
Declare the sweep uninformative for that surface in the run's coverage record
Supply explicit entry point patterns or fall back to reference-level analysis
forbidden: Report the flagged live code as dead
Quote the sweep's confidence score inside a finding
Treat a structurally guaranteed signal as corroboration

cases.request: Interpret a blocking delete-safety verdict for a symbol whose only importer is its own co-located test.
setup: The verdict string is blocking with a terminal stop rule
The blockers array lists only the symbol's own test and files that the same proposed change removes
expected: Classify every blocker: removed by the same change, the symbol's own test, or an independent consumer
Proceed with the removal proposal because no independent consumer exists
Record the blocker classification in the finding
forbidden: Treat the verdict string as evidence that removal is unsafe
Paraphrase the terminal stop rule as safe
Skip the classification and drop the removal candidate
